about: What the FY2026 school general fund ledger at period 13 shows was left unspent, against the range the period-12 ledger allowed and what the School Committee was told in July 2026.

category_rules.label: Counselors & psychologists
category_rules.rule: salary lines, functions 2700–2899 (guidance, social workers, psychologists)

category_rules.label: Administrators & office staff
category_rules.rule: salary lines, functions 1000–2299 (central office, directors, principals, secretaries)

category_rules.label: Nurses, coaches & other staff
category_rules.rule: every other salary line (nurses, athletics, advisors, reserves)

category_rules.label: Out-of-district tuition
category_rules.rule: functions 9000 and up (private and collaborative special-education tuition)

category_rules.label: Special-ed contracted services
category_rules.rule: non-salary lines, functions 2310 and 2320 (contracted therapists, evaluations, tutoring)

category_rules.label: Transportation
category_rules.rule: non-salary lines, function 3300 (regular and special-education buses)

category_rules.label: Building & grounds upkeep
category_rules.rule: every other non-salary line in functions 4000–4999 (repairs, contracted maintenance, custodial and grounds supplies)

category_rules.label: Equipment & technology

benefits.causes: fewer employees enrolled in the health plan than budgeted, staff opting out, or premiums below the estimate
benefits.settles: health-plan enrolment by month and the premium rates

buildings.causes: maintenance projects postponed or not started, a shortage of facilities staff to run them, or a deliberate hold on spending
buildings.settles: the facilities work-order and project list with dates

counselors.causes: a counselor or psychologist post vacant or on leave for part of the year, or the work bought from a contractor instead
counselors.settles: the position-control roster by month for functions 2710 and 2800

other_staff.causes: stipends not paid for seasons or programs that did not run, or a nurse post vacant for part of the year
other_staff.settles: the stipend and nursing payroll by month

paras.causes: aides hired late or not at all, or aides paid from a grant instead
paras.settles: paraprofessional payroll by month and by funding source

sped_services.causes: more children needing contracted therapy or evaluation than budgeted, or contractors covering for vacant staff posts
sped_services.settles: the contracted-service invoices by service type

supplies.causes: a deliberate hold on purchasing, or purchases made from grants and revolving funds instead
supplies.settles: the general-fund journal detail by month

teachers.causes: a post left vacant or filled late, a leave of absence covered for less than the salary, or teachers hired at a lower step than budgeted
teachers.settles: the district’s position-control roster by month: each budgeted post, who held it, from when, and at what step

transport.causes: route or contract prices above budget, or special-education routes added mid-year
transport.settles: the transportation contract and the route list by month

tuition.causes: fewer children placed than budgeted, placements starting later, a placement paid from the circuit breaker fund instead, or a placement billed to a different tuition line
tuition.settles: the placement list by setting, with start dates and the tuition invoice for each

utilities.causes: weather, energy prices, or a bill for one year paid in another

conclusions.basis: `munis-school-ytd.csv`, FY2026 period 13, accounts 535019 and 535023 (spent and committed), and fund 2640 tuition; the district's FY2027 workbook (`lps-budget-lines.csv`), Balanced column, tied to the MUNIS FY2026 original appropriation.
conclusions.claim: FY27 budgets $700,142 for out-of-district tuition; FY26 spent $1,202,771 on the same lines.
conclusions.detail: FY27 sits $502,629 below FY26 on these two lines. Collaborative tuition alone was voted $302,663 for FY26, spent $736,770, and is budgeted $163,742 for FY27; private tuition is budgeted $536,400. Every FY27 scenario carries the same tuition figure, so it is the district's estimate, not one of the cuts. Readings that fit, none tested here: placements that end, more expected from the circuit breaker, or FY27 tuition paid in advance out of FY26.
conclusions.not_shown: How many children each figure pays for, or for which months. A dollar is not a placement (rule 7).
conclusions.so_what: The circuit breaker paid $333,495 on top. The FY28 line has to say which figure it plans from.

conclusions.basis: `munis-school-ytd.csv`, FY2023 to FY2026 period 13, gf-school, available_budget below zero; School Committee minutes, 29 July 2026, the ten transfers listed.
conclusions.claim: 57 school accounts closed FY26 $1,201,434 past their revised budgets; FY25 closed with 4.
conclusions.detail: FY25 closed $22,275 over, with 91 accounts spent to exactly their budget against 29 in FY26. Five accounts carry $811,010 of the FY26 overruns. The school appropriation is one bottom-line total, so a line past its budget is not past the appropriation; but the line budgets are what the next budget is built from. Whether more transfers will post is not shown.

o26.unit: past revised budgets at the FY2026 close

conclusions.not_shown: Whether any line overran by decision or by surprise, and whether the year-end transfer schedule is complete.
conclusions.so_what: The 29 July transfers moved $148,364. FY23 and FY24 closed like FY26, with 70 and 52 over.

conclusions.basis: `munis-school-ytd.csv`, FY2026 period 13; the district's FY2027 workbook, TOTAL ACTUALS & BUDGET row, Level Service and Balanced columns.
conclusions.claim: FY26 left $482,118 unspent; the FY27 school budget was set $761,000 below level service.
conclusions.detail: The floor is 63.4% of the gap between the FY27 balanced and level-service budgets; with every open order released, $718,885 would be 94.5%. The two were not known together: the FY27 budget was set in March 2026, and this surplus was measured in October.
conclusions.not_shown: What free cash the Town will certify, and whether any of it will be appropriated to the schools.
conclusions.so_what: The surplus goes to the town as free cash, and Town Meeting decides where certified free cash is spent.

conclusions.basis: `munis-school-ytd.csv`, FY2023 to FY2026 period 13, accounts 521011 and 535012, original appropriation against spent and committed; the FY2027 workbook, Balanced column.
conclusions.claim: Electricity and contracted therapy ran past their voted budgets all 4 years, by $489,283.
conclusions.detail: Electricity: $303,102 past its voted budgets over the 4 years. Contracted related services (special-education therapy) was voted $103,000 in every one of them and ran $186,181 past. At the Finance Committee in February a member raised the solar panels; nothing here says what they save.

ctot.unit: spent past the voted budget, FY2023 to FY2026

conclusions.not_shown: Why: usage, rates, or more children needing therapy all fit. A dollar is not a kilowatt-hour or a child.
conclusions.so_what: FY27 budgets them at $316,250 and $130,000; FY26 already paid $319,109 and $204,758.

conclusions.basis: `munis-school-ytd.csv`, FY2026 period 13: accounts with transfers_adjustments above zero and available_budget above zero; School Committee minutes, 5 November 2025 and 29 July 2026.
conclusions.claim: 20 accounts were given $117,626 by transfer in FY26 and still ended $223,361 under.
conclusions.detail: Building contracted services received $31,291 and ended $75,660 under. The July minutes record $11,000 moved out of heating; the ledger shows $11,024 moved into heating, net, and it ended $45,560 under. The ledger is net per account and cannot say where any transfer came from.

gleft.unit: left unspent in accounts that received transfers

conclusions.not_shown: When in the year each transfer was made, or whether the invoice was paid from another line.
conclusions.so_what: School Committee dues got $13,500 for a search invoice and ended with $13,689 unspent.

conclusions.basis: `munis-school-ytd.csv`, FY2023 to FY2026 period 13: gf-school functions 9000 and up, and fund 2640 (special-school) functions 9000 and up, spent and committed.
conclusions.claim: The circuit breaker paid 21.7% of FY26 out-of-district tuition; in FY23 it paid 61.9%.
conclusions.detail: Tuition from both funds was $799,715 in FY23 and $1,536,266 in FY26. A general-fund line can rise because the cost rose or because another fund paid less, and the two look identical (rule 11).

cb26.unit: of out-of-district tuition paid by the circuit breaker

conclusions.not_shown: The circuit breaker's balance, and how much of each year's reimbursement was already committed when it arrived.
conclusions.so_what: Over the same years the general fund's tuition bill went from $304,748 to $1,202,771.

conclusions.basis: `munis-school-ytd.csv`, FY2023 to FY2026 period 13, the supplies and building-upkeep categories of `CATEGORIES`, original appropriation against spent and committed.
conclusions.claim: Supplies and services were voted above what they spent in all 4 years, $375,175 in all.
conclusions.detail: Upkeep was voted $332,016 in FY23 and $652,033 in FY26. A line left under its vote every year reads as budgeted high as much as run lean; this is the most thrift could explain, not a finding that it did.

sup.unit: voted above spending, FY2023 to FY2026

conclusions.not_shown: Whether anyone chose to spend less; the monthly journal would show it and is not published.
conclusions.so_what: Building upkeep's vote rose 96.4% from FY23 to FY26; FY26 spent $156,984 less than voted.

conclusions.basis: `munis-school-ytd.csv`, FY2026 period 13, account 0100-3-300-2800-07-2-06-1-511023 and the two kindergarten accounts; the FY2027 workbook rows 359 and 332, 333.
conclusions.claim: A $98,784 psychologist line paid nobody in FY26; FY27 budgets the line at $102,227.
conclusions.detail: Both are measured in the same two documents: the period-13 ledger for FY26 and the district's FY27 workbook, Balanced column. A budget line is not a post: neither shows who was employed, or whether the work was paid from another line or fund.

pv.unit: voted for the primary school psychologist line, FY2026

conclusions.not_shown: Whether the psychologist post was vacant, on leave, or paid elsewhere; what the kindergarten aides were hired to do.
conclusions.so_what: Kindergarten aides went the other way: $99,064 paid against no budget, and FY27 budgets none.

conclusions.basis: `munis-school-ytd.csv`, FY2023 to FY2026 period 13, the five 2330 special-education aide accounts and health insurance (570001); the FY2027 workbook, Balanced column.
conclusions.claim: Credit: FY27 budgets special-ed aides $297,321 above what FY26 paid them, after an overrun.
conclusions.detail: The five special-education aide lines ran $111,018 past their revised budgets in FY26 and spent $1,526,467; FY27 budgets $1,823,788. Health insurance closed FY26 2.1% under its budget, close to the line after two years short.

pa.unit: FY2027 special-education aide budget above FY2026 spending

conclusions.not_shown: Whether FY27's aide budget matches the posts the district will fill.
conclusions.so_what: Health insurance, $328,771 short over FY23 and FY24, closed FY26 $78,313 under its budget.

conclusions.basis: `munis-school-ytd.csv`, FY2026 period 13, salary lines (object 51xxxx) by category; School Committee minutes, 29 July 2026.
conclusions.claim: Salary lines left $192,211 net, though paraprofessionals ran $208,082 over.
conclusions.detail: Counselors & psychologists left $191,162 and teachers & substitutes $167,992. The 29 July 2026 minutes say money in a special-education teacher account "was associated with a leave of absence", and was moved to cover paraprofessional overages. Vacancies, leaves and hiring steps all fit the rest; the position-control roster would settle it.

s_net.unit: left over in salary lines, net

conclusions.not_shown: Which posts were vacant or on leave, and for how long. A dollar is not a post (rule 7, rule 11).
conclusions.so_what: The record names one leave of absence; no document here says why counselor money was left.

conclusions.basis: `sources/data/munis-school-ytd.csv`, FY2026 period 13, report gf-school, type E; `sources/data/munis-ledger.csv`, FY2026 period 12, department 300; joined account by account on org and object.
conclusions.claim: The FY26 school surplus stands at $482,118, $16.95 more than the June ledger showed.
conclusions.detail: The period-12 report run on 1 September 2026 allowed the year to close anywhere between $482,101 and $718,885. The period-13 report run on 6 October 2026 lands at the bottom of that range: the only change between them is $16.95 of a purchase order released in one supplies account.
conclusions.not_shown: Whether period 13 is complete: the report was run while purchase orders were still open.
conclusions.so_what: Not one of the 258 accounts in both runs changed its spending between them.

conclusions.basis: `munis-school-ytd.csv`, FY2026 and FY2025 period 13, the encumbrances column, department 300.
conclusions.claim: $236,767 is still committed to open purchase orders, across 27 accounts.
conclusions.detail: The two largest are electricity charges ($62,362) and collaborative tuitions ($58,708). The FY2025 report of the same department, run the same day, shows $0 encumbered: that year is fully closed and this one is not.
conclusions.not_shown: Which orders will be paid, released, or carried into the next year.
conclusions.so_what: Paid, the surplus stays at $482,118; released, it can rise to at most $718,885.

conclusions.basis: School Committee minutes, 29 July 2026, pages 3 to 4; `munis-school-ytd.csv`, FY2026 period 13.
conclusions.claim: In July the Committee heard FY26 would return well below FY25’s $600,000.
conclusions.detail: The minutes of 29 July 2026 record the business manager as "confident the remaining amount would be well below that figure" — the FY25 return, put at about 2.5% of the budget. As a share of FY26’s revised budget the floor is 1.8% and the ceiling 2.7%. Whether the statement holds depends on the open purchase orders.

stated.unit: returned in FY25, as stated in the minutes

conclusions.not_shown: What the business manager meant by "that figure", the dollars or the share; and a minute is a summary, not a transcript.
conclusions.so_what: The floor, $482,118, is below it; the ceiling, $718,885, is above it.

grain: DOLLARS, department 300 (school general fund) only, FY2026 period 13 as run on 6 October 2026, 415 accounts — compared account by account with the period-12 run of 1 September 2026. Not a comparison of budget to actual: one ledger at two periods.
not_established: Why any category was left under budget. The ledger shows where money was left; vacancies, placements, prices and restraint all produce the same rows.
Whether anyone chose to spend less. The discretionary share is the most thrift could explain, not a finding that it did; the monthly journal would show it and is not published.
Whether the $236,767 still encumbered will be paid, released, or carried into FY2027.
Where the $85,090 moved into the department during the year came from — net per account, no counterparty.
What "expense accounts" meant in the 29 July 2026 minutes, and so whether the ledger agrees with "approximately 100.2% expended".
Why operations & maintenance was left unspent — dollars are not posts.
What the FY2027 out-of-district tuition budget assumes: which placements, for which months, and how much the circuit breaker is expected to pay.
Whether further FY2026 year-end transfers will post against the accounts still past their revised budgets, and from which lines.
Where any FY2026 transfer came from or went to: the ledger is net per account.
Why electricity has run past its voted budget in every year held.
What was said under "FY26 Year End Budget review" on 2 September 2026 and 9 September 2026: no minutes for either meeting are held.
